issues.description: The dialogue models 'should' (statement and question) but never 'shouldn't', and the grammar note mentions 'shouldn't' without giving an example. Learners see only half of the stated grammar point in use.
issues.suggested_fix: Add a short example to the grammar note, e.g. "You shouldn't go to work today.", or, if time allows, add a line such as Anna: 'You shouldn't work today.'

issues.description: The gloss for 'headache' ('a bad feeling in your head') is vague; a 'bad feeling' could mean sadness or worry. 'Pain' is an A2-level word and is clearer.
issues.suggested_fix: Change the gloss to 'a pain in your head'.

issues.description: The spec theme is 'feeling sick and visiting the pharmacy', but the episode only covers feeling sick; there is no pharmacy element. Acceptable within the 10-15 second micro_dialogue limit, but the theme is only partially realised.
issues.suggested_fix: Optional: change Ben's last line to 'Should I go to the pharmacy?' or accept the narrower scope and adjust the theme wording.

qa_report.summary: A clean, accurate A2 micro_dialogue. All four lines are grammatical and natural, every word is at or below level, the target word 'headache' and review words 'doctor' and 'sick' are all used, and 'should' for advice is modelled correctly in both a statement and a question. Three minor points: 'shouldn't' is named in the grammar note but never exemplified, the 'headache' gloss ('a bad feeling in your head') is vaguer than necessary, and the pharmacy half of the theme is not represented. No critical or major issues.
